uncited: Volume-peeling operates in a multi-pass pipeline that interleaves geometry peeling with volumetric ray-casting.
*   Scene containing translucent polygonal geometry and volumetric data.
**Initialization Pass:** Render sections of the volume that are *not* enclosed within any translucent geometry.
**Geometry Peeling Pass:** Perform a dual depth peeling pass on the translucent geometry.
This computes the color and depth of the front and back layers (peels) of the geometry in a single render pass.
**Volumetric Peel Pass:** Invoke the volume mapper in an additional render pass.
Use the entry and exit depth points obtained from the most recent geometry peel as the boundaries for ray-casting through the volume.
**Iteration:** Repeat steps 2-4 for subsequent layers of geometry peels until all layers are processed or the maximum number of peels is reached.
*   **Time Complexity:** Performance depends on geometry complexity and ray-sampling distance.

The mention of 'depth buffers for peeling' is supported by the description of using 'updated depths to feed the next pair of peels' and the general concept of depth peeling relying on depth buffers to determine visibility and ordering.
